quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders not rely only on mirrors to see around them?

options.text: Motorcycle mirrors are smaller than car mirrors, so you cannot see as much.
Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars do.
Mirrors are never accurate.
Mirrors take your eyes off the road and should never be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars do.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. You cannot rely on mirrors alone to see what is behind you. Check your blind spots frequently by turning your head.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.
Apply the brake on the tire that is flat.
Apply both brakes.
Do not use either brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, slowly apply the brake on the tire that is not flat, if you know which one it is.

questions.question: When you are about to pass another vehicle on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the right part of your lane.
Ride in the left part of your lane.
Get as close as possible to the vehicle in front of you.
Do not signal, as it may distract the driver you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the left part of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane when passing. Signal your intention and check for traffic. Pass when it is safe. Signal again and return to your original lane when you can.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: To reduce crash risk, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Be visible.
Communicate your intentions.
Be ready to react to hazards.
Hope another driver sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope another driver sees you.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make yourself visible and signal your intentions clearly. Keep space around you and watch for hazards. Do not depend on hoping other drivers will see you.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.

options.text: Always
Usually
Frequently
Seldom

questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: You will seldom hear your tire go flat. Usually, a change in how your motorcycle handles tells you that a tire has failed.

questions.question: If your motorcycle begins to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Keep riding, as the wobble will correct itself.
Brake quickly.
Close the throttle to slow down.
Speed up quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the throttle to slow down.
questions.explanation: Do not accelerate during a wobble. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly and close the throttle to slow down. Lean forward and pull off the road as soon as you can. Then find and fix what caused the wobble.

questions.question: To prevent fatigue on a long ride, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Dress warmly.
Limit how far you ride each day.
Take breaks often.
Take artificial stimulants.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take artificial stimulants.
questions.explanation: Protect yourself from wind and rain by dressing properly. Ride no more than about six hours per day. Stop for a break at least every two hours. Avoid artificial stimulants because you may become very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: For routine braking, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Alternate between the front and rear brakes to make them last longer.
Always use both the front and rear brakes together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use both the front and rear brakes together.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When a driver makes eye contact with you:

options.text: It means they see you.
It will never happen.
It does not mean they will yield to you.
It guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume a driver will yield to you just because they make eye contact. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but do not actually notice them.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, what should you usually do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the handlebars firmly. Ease off the throttle and keep riding straight. If you must brake, slowly apply the brake of the good tire. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: It is not necessary if you have a windshield.
It only protects your eyes.
It protects more than just your eyes.
It does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects more than just your eyes.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for either one.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Keep other drivers from sharing your lane.
Allow you to see scenery better.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Hide your intentions from other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep other drivers from sharing your lane.
questions.explanation: The right lane position helps you stay safe. It keeps you out of other vehicles' blind spots, helps you see and be seen better, helps you avoid hazards on the road, helps you avoid wind blasts from other vehicles, and gives you an escape route. Position yourself so other drivers won't try to share your lane.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, where should you ride?

options.text: In the part of your lane that lets other drivers see you as soon as possible.
Always in the left lane to be farther from oncoming traffic.
Slowly creep up to the intersection.
Weave slightly so your headlight is more likely to be spotted.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the part of your lane that lets other drivers see you as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, position your motorcycle so oncoming drivers can see you as early as possible. For example, when approaching a blind corner on your right, ride in the left part of your lane, not the center.

questions.question: What should a passenger never do?

options.text: Wear a helmet.
Lean when the operator leans.
Wear tight clothing.
Ride sidesaddle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride sidesaddle.
questions.explanation: In South Carolina, passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection. All riders should wear helmets and eye protection. Passengers should wear snug clothing that won't catch on the motorcycle. Passengers must lean with the operator during turns. Passengers must never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: In a normal turn, how should the motorcycle and rider lean?

options.text: They should lean together at the same angle.
They should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should not.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should not.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should lean together at the same angle.
questions.explanation: During normal turns, the motorcycle and rider should lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: When riding over rough surfaces, how should you hold the handgrips?

options.text: Loosely to allow for movement.
Firmly to maintain control.
Use lots of throttle to help you cross the rough surface.
Ride without a helmet so it doesn't cover your face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Firmly to maintain control.
questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly when riding over rough surfaces. This helps you keep control of your motorcycle and steer safely.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular in shape?

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs and other regulatory signs are rectangular. They have white backgrounds with black letters or symbols. You must follow all rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: If you shift into a lower gear while going too fast, what happens?

options.text: The motorcycle could jerk and the rear tire could skid.
The motorcycle could accelerate too quickly.
The front tire will likely skid.
The engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle could jerk and the rear tire could skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift into a lower gear while traveling too fast, the motorcycle will jerk and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: Why is a flat front tire especially dangerous?

options.text: It affects your steering.
The front tire provides power, so you lose acceleration.
The flat tire will shake the bike and make it hard to see your mirrors.
You won't be able to use the brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It affects your steering.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is very dangerous because it affects your ability to steer. If your front tire goes flat while riding, safely get off the road as quickly as possible.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a safe way to prevent fatigue while riding?

options.text: Protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain.
Take artificial stimulants.
Limit how far you ride in one day.
Take frequent breaks to rest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take artificial stimulants.
questions.explanation: On long trips, take frequent breaks to rest. Do not ride more than six hours in one day. Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain, as these make you tire quickly. Never take artificial stimulants. When they wear off, the effects can be very dangerous.

questions.question: As a beginning rider, what should you do when following another vehicle?

options.text: Keep at least four seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Get as close to the other vehicle as possible.
Do not worry about following distance.
Always ride on the left side of the lane so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep at least four seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Beginning riders should keep at least four seconds of following distance. Increase this distance if conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: Why should motorcyclists in a group avoid riding in pairs?

options.text: A merging driver may not see both riders.
Reflections from helmets may make it hard for riders to see.
Riding in pairs does not give riders enough space to avoid hazards.
Riders on the left side cannot easily exit a highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in pairs does not give riders enough space to avoid hazards.
questions.explanation: When traveling in a group, motorcyclists should not ride in pairs. Neither rider will have enough room to maneuver and avoid hazards.

questions.question: Switching to a lower gear is also called:

options.text: Engine braking.
Acceleration.
Upshifting.
Coasting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Engine braking.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear works like braking. This is why downshifting is called engine braking.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Give you a good view of the shoulder.
Give you a poor view of road hazards.
Allow others to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
questions.explanation: Choose your lane position to see others and be seen by them. Do not ride in another driver's blind spot for long periods.
